q: Counting sort on n values in the range 0..K costs…
why: One pass to count (n), one pass over the counts (K).

q: How can counting sort beat the O(n log n) limit for sorting?
options: It uses a faster CPU trick
It never compares elements; values are used as array indexes
It only works on sorted input
why: The n log n lower bound applies to comparison sorts only.

q: In cyclic sort for values 1..n, where does value 7 go?
why: Value v belongs at index v − 1.

q: After swapping nums[i] to its home, why not advance i immediately?
options: The value just swapped into index i may also need to move
why: Keep placing whatever lands at i until it's home or is a duplicate.

q: What does this return for nums = [3, 0, 1]?
why: Expected sum of 0..3 is 6, actual sum is 4.

q: Values are up to 10⁹ and n = 10⁵. Is counting sort a good idea?
options: No: the count array would need 10⁹ slots
why: Counting sort only pays off when the value range is small compared to memory.
